prompt: Which of these Terraform commands ran fully in the lab, with no Azure credentials?
hint: Which ones only read the files and the provider's schema?

choices.text: terraform plan
choices.why: Plan asks Resource Manager what exists, and stopped at the sign-in.

choices.text: terraform validate
choices.why: Right. It checks the configuration against the provider's schema, locally.

choices.text: terraform init with the azurerm backend
choices.why: The backend needs the Storage API, and stopped at the sign-in too.

choices.text: terraform apply
choices.why: Apply changes Azure; nothing in the lab can.

hint: One is a record, the other is what it records.

choices.text: The lock file is small, and Git refuses directories
choices.why: Git stores directories fine; the reason is what each one is.

choices.text: `.terraform/` holds the state, which must stay private
choices.why: The state is in the backend; `.terraform/` holds the downloaded provider.

choices.text: The lock records versions and checksums; .terraform holds 254 MB of downloads
choices.why: Right. Everyone installs the same bytes from the record, and nobody commits the bytes.

choices.text: The lock file stops two people applying at once
choices.why: That is the state lock, a lease in the backend; this file pins providers.

prompt: Why does the azurerm provider require `subscription_id` since version 4?
hint: What would it otherwise have to do?

choices.text: So it never guesses which subscription to change
choices.why: Right. A default subscription is somebody's last `az account set`.

choices.text: Because resource group names are unique per subscription
choices.why: True, and not the reason the provider insists.

choices.text: To bill Terraform's own usage to that subscription
choices.why: Terraform is not billed by Azure.

choices.text: Because OIDC tokens carry no tenant
choices.why: The tenant comes separately; the subscription is a different question.

prompt: Reading the lab's `terraform plan` error from the right, what is the first thing that failed?
hint: The innermost cause is at the end.

choices.text: Building an authoriser for Resource Manager
choices.why: That is the outermost failure, the consequence of the others.

choices.text: Reaching the Terraform Registry
choices.why: The provider was already installed by init.

choices.text: The Azure command line had no sign-in
choices.why: Right. `Please run 'az login'` is the innermost cause; everything else follows.

choices.text: Parsing the subscription id
choices.why: The id was accepted; the tenant could not be found.

prompt: Match each place Terraform runs to the way it should sign in.
hint: Three places, three mechanisms, none of them a stored secret.

pairs.left: A self-hosted agent VM in Azure

right_distractors: A client secret in the provider block

prompt: Why does the shop keep the state account in `rg-tfstate`, managed by no Terraform configuration?
hint: What could the shop's own configuration one day delete?

choices.text: Storage accounts cannot share a group with app resources
choices.why: They can; the separation is a decision about risk.

choices.text: So the configuration that might delete rg-shop never owns its own record
choices.why: Right. A destroy cannot take the state with it.

choices.text: To get a cheaper price for state blobs
choices.why: Price is per account and data, not per resource group.

choices.text: Because backends refuse accounts in other groups
choices.why: The backend names any group you like.

prompt: The backend block leaves out `use_azuread_auth`. What changes, and why does the shop care?
hint: What does the backend use instead of your identity?

choices.text: Nothing; the backend always uses the signed-in identity
choices.why: Without the setting it fetches the account key.

choices.text: State becomes unencrypted at rest
choices.why: Encryption at rest does not depend on how the backend authenticates.

choices.text: Locking stops working
choices.why: Leases work with either way of signing in.

choices.text: It uses the account key, so key holders read every state
choices.why: Right. State holds every value Terraform knows, so the shop turns key access off.

prompt: `terraform plan` failed on the Resource Manager API and `terraform init` with the backend failed on the Storage API. What does the pair teach?

choices.text: That the backend and the provider use different versions of Terraform
choices.why: One Terraform binary ran both.

choices.text: State and resources sit behind separate roles
choices.why: Right. Storage Blob Data Contributor on the account, Contributor on the resource groups.

choices.text: That Azurite answered one of them
choices.why: Neither reached Azurite; the backend block names a real account.

choices.text: That the lab's network blocks storage
choices.why: Both stopped at the sign-in, before any network request to Azure.

prompt: What is the azurerm backend's state lock?

choices.text: A row in a separate locking table
choices.why: No table is needed; that was the S3 backend's old design.

choices.text: A file named terraform.lock next to the state
choices.why: There is no second file; the claim is on the state blob itself.

choices.text: A lease on the state blob
choices.why: Right. While held, nobody else can take it or overwrite the blob.

choices.text: A Resource Manager lock on the storage account
choices.why: Those stop deletion of the account; they are lesson 7's subject.

prompt: Acquiring a lease on a blob that already has one fails with the error code Lease___.
A pipeline was cancelled during `terraform apply`, and the state is now locked. What does the shop do before running `terraform force-unlock`?
hint: What does breaking a lease not check?

choices.text: Waits sixty seconds for the lease to expire
choices.why: Terraform's lease has no time limit; it was infinite in the transcript.

choices.text: Deletes the state blob and uploads a fresh one
choices.why: That destroys the record; nothing about a lock calls for it.

choices.text: Confirms the holder is really gone
choices.why: Right. Breaking frees the blob whether or not somebody is still writing.

choices.text: Adds force-unlock to the pipeline's retry step
choices.why: That is exactly what the shop's rule forbids.

prompt: Put what the shop's pipeline does with Terraform in order.
hint: Local checks first, then Azure, then the lock.
items: plan takes the lease, reads the state and the resources
trap: Signing in before the local checks is the slip: they need no identity and fail faster.

prompt: Which of these protect the shop's state? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Blob versioning on the state account
choices.why: Yes. Lesson 7 restores from it.

choices.text: Turning off key access on the account
choices.why: Yes. Only identities with the data role can read it.

choices.text: The lease taken during plan and apply
choices.why: Yes. Two runs cannot write it at once.

choices.text: Committing terraform.tfstate to the repository as a backup
choices.why: No. It holds every value Terraform knows, sensitive ones included.
